What I assume: this is a London/US-based investment-banking/valuation-style analyst final round; you'll face technical modeling/valuation, transaction story/fit, and behavioral/fit with partners. If any of that is off, tell me.
One-page prep plan (use these in the interview, aloud and for notes)
1) Opening 30 seconds
- Brief intro: current role + 2 bullets: (a) deal/transaction or project that shows relevant technical work and (b) a strength that matches Lincoln (execution, attention to detail, client communication). End with: “I’m excited about Lincoln because [specific: mid-market focus / cross-border M&A / sector X] and want to bring [your top skill].”
2) Technical (be crisp, show process)
- Valuation fundamentals: be ready to walk comparables, precedent transactions, and DCF at a 1–2 minute level each: what it answers, the key inputs, and main weaknesses of each method.
- DCF short checklist to speak through: forecast free cash flow (revenue growth drivers, margins), choose explicit period (3–5 years for analyst-level?), terminal value method (exit multiple vs. Gordon growth), discount rate (WACC — explain components briefly), and sensitivity table (show +/- on terminal multiple and WACC). If asked to compute, do high-level math: NPV direction, importance of FCF profile.
- LBO basics (if asked): sources & uses, pro forma equity check, IRR drivers (entry multiple, deleveraging, margin expansion), common modeling shortcuts.
- Accounting: reconcile Net Income → Unlevered FCF (addbacks: D&A; subtract capex and change in working capital; tax effects). Be prepared to explain a one-line balance sheet movement (e.g., why AR rise hurts cash).
- Short math tests: practice quick mental math and % change logic. Speak your steps.
3) Transaction discussion (how to tell a deal story)
- Format: Situation → Your role & actions → Outcome (with numbers).
- If they ask about a deal you worked on: open with the one-sentence summary (industry, buyer/seller, size), then 3 technical actions you owned (modeling, due diligence, management materials) and the impact (timing saved, number of questions resolved, valuation move).
- Anticipate follow-ups on what you worked on day-to-day — have 2 specific examples: a modeling error you found/fixed or a client question you answered with an analysis.
4) Fit / behavioral (prepare 4 STAR stories)
- Teamwork under pressure: cross-check model under tight deadline.
- Mistake + learning: a modeling/data error, what you did to correct and the process you changed.
- Client interaction: an instance you communicated technical info to a non-technical stakeholder.
- Motivation for Lincoln & stay story: why investment banking/mid-market M&A, why Lincoln specifically, and why you’ll stay (learning curve, client exposure). Be specific: mention Lincoln’s sectors, mid-market focus, deal cross-border if relevant.
5) Questions they will often ask and short ways to answer
- Why Lincoln? — 2 specific facts: e.g., firm’s mid-market focus, coverage in [sector they expect], or a recent deal (name it if you know it). Tie to how you add value.
- Walk me through your resume — use 5–7 sentences: education, current role highlights, most relevant deal, why banking next.
- Where do you see yourself in 3–5 years? — growth in transaction roles, senior analyst/associate path, sector specialization.
- Tell me about a time you had conflicting priorities — show prioritization and stakeholder communication.
6) Practical final-round tips
- Mirror the interviewer: if senior banker uses short answers, be concise; if they are conversational, add one-sentence color.
- Bring one printed 1-page deal sheet for the interview: top line deal name, your role, your 2–3 contributions, and a quantifiable outcome.
- Ask 3 good questions at the end (rotate): recent biggest challenge winning or closing deals; team structure day-to-day; what makes someone successful there in first 12 months.
- If asked for numbers or assumptions, say them aloud, show reasoning, and check if they want a different assumption.
7) Quick drills to run now (30–60 minutes)
- Draft 30s intro and 60–90s deal story for your top deal. Practice out loud twice.
- Rehearse a one-minute DCF explanation and one-minute comparables explanation.
- Run 3 STAR stories aloud; tighten them to 45–60 seconds each.
- Do 10 quick mental math questions (percent changes, multiplication by factors) to warm up.

If you want, I can:
- Quiz you now with 6 mock final-round questions (technical + behavioral) and score each answer; or
- Rewrite your 30s intro and one deal STAR story if you paste them.

One short question: which market is the role in (city/country) and which sector did they say the role covers?

You don't have any applications or a queued posting on file yet. The one step that starts this is: pick a specific job posting for me (paste the posting link or tell me the company + exact title and city).

What I will prepare for the first application, exactly — field by field — and what I will fill versus what I will ask you to confirm:

1) Posting reference
- What I will show: company name, exact job title, location, and the posting link you supplied (or the employer's posting ID if you named it). 
- What I will need from you: nothing extra unless the posting is ambiguous; if so I'll ask which posting you meant.
2) Resume / contact used at top of application
- What I will fill: the name and email exactly as you saved for your resume contact. 
- What I will need from you: if you haven't provided the exact name and email to use, I'll ask: "What name and email should go at the top of your resume?"

3) Resume PDF attached
- What I will include: a tailored resume PDF built from your confirmed profile facts only. 
- What I will need from you: you must have confirmed the facts used in the resume; if not, I will leave bracketed fields and ask you to confirm them before creating the PDF.
4) Cover note / short answer (the brief tailored paragraph some forms call "Why you" or the cover letter field)
- What I will draft: one concise paragraph (<=120 words) tailored to the posting that states your top relevant accomplishment(s) and why you want the role. I will leave [brackets] for any missing personal detail (dates, numbers, specific metrics). 
- What I will need from you: confirm or replace any bracketed items and approve the paragraph.
5) Full cover letter (optional PDF)
- What I will prepare if you request it: a 1-page cover letter expanded from the short cover note; otherwise omitted. 
- What I will need from you: any particular story or detail you want emphasized, or approval to use the short note only.
6) Application form fields (the line-by-line fields the employer asks)
For each field I will either fill it from your confirmed facts or leave a bracketed prompt. Typical fields:
- Full name: filled from your saved resume contact (or left blank if none saved).
- Email: filled from your saved resume contact.
- Phone: left blank unless you provide it to save.
- Current city / address: filled from confirmed location fact or left as [city].
- LinkedIn URL: left blank unless you provide it.
- Work authorization / visa status: filled only if you have a confirmed fact; otherwise left as [work authorization].
- Earliest start date: left as [earliest start date] for you to confirm.
- Salary expectations / current salary: left blank unless you give the exact text to include; I will not guess.
- Remote / onsite preference: filled from a confirmed preference or left as [remote/on-site/hybrid].
- Portfolio / GitHub / other links: included only if you provided them.

7) Screening questions and short answers
- What I will draft: concise, tailored answers for any employer screening questions, each with a clear result or metric where possible. Missing facts remain in [brackets].
- What I will need from you: confirm any bracketed facts or provide a short fact (e.g., a metric, a specific tool you used).
8) Documents to attach beyond resume
- What I will include if you supply them: certificates, transcripts, portfolio files exactly as you provide.
- What I will need from you: upload or paste the files or confirm they exist as a fact.

9) Recruiter or outreach email (if an email contact is available and you want one)
- What I will draft: a short <120-word email to the recruiter or hiring address with one tailored sentence and the resume attached. It will remain a draft for you to send.
- What I will need from you: the recruiter's email (if you have it) and the sign-off you want saved.
10) Internal prep notes (visible on the application card for your review)
- What I will write: 3 lines — (1) why you fit, (2) top 1–2 gaps vs the posting, (3) one interview question to practice.
- What I will need from you: none; these are for you to review.

11) Submission settings and final checks (what I will display before queueing)
- What I will show: which resume persona will be used, whether a cover note or cover letter is attached, which contact info is used, and a list of any blocking missing items (unconfirmed facts, missing phone, missing files).
- What I will need from you: your approval on the card in the extension. Nothing is sent without your explicit approval.
12) Confirmation line after you approve (what you will see)
- What I will show: "Prepared: [Company] — [Title]. Resume: [resume name]. Attachments: [list]. Missing: [list]. Ready to submit on your device." I will only queue it; submission happens when you use the extension on your device.

Assumptions I used where you haven't told me:
- You have not yet given a resume contact (name/email), confirmed profile facts, or posted a job link. I will leave bracketed prompts for any of these missing items on the card.
- I will not send any email or submit anything without your explicit approval in the extension.
Next step: paste the job posting link (or give the company + exact title + city) you want me to prepare the first application for. One question: do you want a full one-page cover letter attached to this first application, or only the short cover paragraph (yes = full letter, no = short paragraph)?
